transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Yes—often worth repairing. A 12-year-old Henry is usually a good candidate because they’re simple, robust machines and parts are widely available.

Before assuming motor trouble, check the easy causes:

1. Unplug it.
2. Remove the hose, tubes and floor head and check for blockages (especially bends in the hose and the floor head).
3. Check the bag’s cardboard/rubber collar is fully seated on the inlet—not folded or partly off.
4. Make sure the filter basket/filter is fitted correctly and the lid seals properly.
5. Briefly run it with just the hose removed:
• Normal sound and strong suction: blockage is in hose/tube/head.
• Still weak and rattly/growly: likely inside the machine—motor bearings, carbon brushes, or possibly debris/damage around the fan.

A rough rattling growl plus reduced suction is more concerning than the usual “bag full” tone. I’d stop using it if there’s a burning smell, excessive heat, smoke, electrical smell, or sparking visible through vents; a failing motor can worsen quickly.

### Is it economical?
Generally:
• Simple blockage, seal, switch, cable, filter issue: definitely repair.
• Brushes or a minor motor/fan issue: usually worth it.
• Replacement motor fitted professionally: worth considering if the total is roughly under half to two-thirds of a new Henry’s price.

Typical UK-style ballpark costs can be around £50–£100 for a motor part or roughly £100–£180+ supplied and fitted, depending on the repairer and model. A new Henry is often not vastly more than that, so get a quote first—but don’t write it off solely because it is 12 years old.

A vacuum repair shop can normally diagnose it very quickly. Tell them: “weak suction even with new bag/filter, and a rattly/growling motor noise.” That will point them straight toward an airflow blockage versus motor/fan/bearing problem.

Thank you. I fitted a genuine new bag and a new cloth filter last week, and a coin drops straight through the hose, so I don't think it's a blockage. Since you mention a burning smell and sparks, I'm afraid there is a hot, burning electrical smell after about five minutes of running. In a dim hall I also saw sparks flickering inside through the vents on top. Should I keep using it?

No—stop using it immediately and unplug it.

A hot electrical/burning smell plus visible sparking and a rough, weak sound strongly suggests a failing motor, carbon brushes/commutator, or possibly damaged wiring. Continuing to run it risks:

• Motor failure and further internal damage
• Overheating or melting insulation/plastic
• Electric shock risk if wiring is compromised
• In the worst case, fire

Do not keep testing it “just briefly,” and don’t leave it plugged in. Remove the plug from the socket and keep it somewhere dry until it can be inspected.

It may still be repairable—Henry motors/brush assemblies are commonly serviceable or replaceable—but it needs a vacuum/appliance repairer or a competent person to inspect it before it is used again. Given it is 12 years old, ask for a diagnosis and quote; if the motor and/or wiring need replacement, compare that with a new machine or a professionally refurbished Henry.
